TTL-expired selffed rows are still dispatchable because _next_work filters only on done_ts and never on status "expired", so rail 5's reap does not stop the 24/7 burn of expired asks

_assert_public_host validates one DNS resolution but opener.open performs a second, independent resolution, so the public-IP check is a check-then-use gap a rebinding resolver on an allowlisted host can pass
selffeed rail-5 TTL expiry reaps rows the verify topic then skips, since its candidate filter requires status == "sensed", so any row expired before sensing can never be verified or drained

t_impfeed's week window uses `ts.timestamp() < cutoff` without normalizing naive parsed timestamps to UTC, so naive ts values are interpreted in local time and the window boundary shifts by the host offset
LEDGER written without atomic tmp+replace risks interleaved/corrupt jsonl under concurrent writes
REPORT written without atomic tmp+replace risks partial/corrupted markdown on crash
catalog() passes bearer token to _fetch without validating ks non-empty, causing IndexError on empty keys
`keys()` reads only two env vars and `call` picks `ks[idx % len(ks)]`, so with one key present all 40 models share it while `k = ks[idx % len(ks)]` gives no rotation across models
Race condition on lane selection in worker() uses unprotected hash on mutable LANES list

lane.conc ramp and ceiling are never enforced; every chore thread calls its lane concurrently with no semaphore, so all chores hit each provider at once and the recorded "wall" measures thread count, not provider limits
Retry fallback re-dispatches a chore to a lane selected by Python's salted `hash()`, which differs per process, so lane assignment is not reproducible and can silently pick the lane that just failed.
`touch_ok` ramps concurrency but nothing ever runs more than one call per lane at a time, so `self.conc` is recorded as a ceiling that was never actually exercised.
Arbitrary code execution: score_exec runs model-generated code via exec() with no sandbox, so any top-level payload in the response executes locally

Verdict logic compares rounded float scores for exact equality and treats any tie (including 0.0-vs-0.0 after errors filtered) as "LOW fine", so a probe where every tier failed still records "LOW fine" in the ledger

`score_design_correct` receives `domain=task_id` ("design"/"design_vague"), a literal string whose words are filtered by `len(w) > 3`, so `hits` is always 0 and `relevant` floors at 0 unless `domain_terms` is empty
Non-atomic overwrite of OUT_MD causes irreversible loss of the anchor map if the script crashes mid-write
known_ids() ignores OUT_JSONL when building the exclusion set, causing duplicate harvests and repeated work across subsequent script runs
